claims.text: No information on cross-contamination controls. The kitchen handles fish, shellfish, and wheat-based soy sauce throughout service with no stated separation protocols.
Standard wheat-containing soy sauce is used for neta glaze and accompaniment — a direct and unavoidable gluten source in the omakase format as served.
The entire menu is fish- and seafood-based; no plant-only preparation stream exists.

No allergy or dietary accommodation policy is published. The fixed omakase format leaves little room for substitution; guests with serious allergies should contact the restaurant directly before booking.

name: 鮨旬美 西川 (Sushi Shunbi Nishikawa)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free preparation area or protocol is documented. In a small 8-seat counter kitchen handling multiple courses simultaneously, cross-contamination from soy sauce and other wheat-containing condiments is essentially certain.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is used in nigiri preparation. No mention of tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternatives in any reviewed source.
Every course involves seafood; fish-bone dashi is used for appetiser preparations. There is no plant-based track and no separation of animal products.
The restaurant's official policy is to decline reservations from guests with severe allergies or broad ingredient restrictions, citing incompatibility with the omakase format.

The TableCheck reservation page explicitly states: 'We cannot accommodate requests if allergic reactions occur due to the use of the same frying oil or cooking utensils, or the manufacturing process.' Shared equipment is confirmed — cross-contamination risk is real.

Standard wheat-containing soy sauce is used throughout the omakase — marinades (漬け maguro), brushed nigiri finishing, and dipping are all standard Edomae practice. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere.
Fish and seafood are the core of every course. Dashi used in the kitchen (including in the adjacent 勝手口 河内屋) is fish-based. No vegan-safe preparation track exists.

Allergy accommodations with ingredient modifications are available per the TableCheck page, but with explicit caveats: shared frying oil and shared cooking utensils are not manageable. Guests with severe allergies should call 052-211-8322 (10:30–19:00) before booking.
Counter format means diners can watch preparation directly and speak with the chef — the best environment to communicate dietary needs in real time.

name: 担々麺専門店 麺屋•高豚 浄心店 (Tantanmen Senmonten Menya Haiton Joshin-ten)

claims.text: Wheat noodles are the core product at every station; airborne flour and shared cooking water make cross-contamination unavoidable.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is the expected seasoning base for the broth; no tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is documented.
All broth is pork-bone based; no plant-based cooking line exists. Cross-contact with pork products is inherent to every dish.

name: 手打そば処 谷屋 (Tebachi Soba-dokoro Taniya)

claims.text: Wheat flour is used daily in the kitchen for standard nibachi (二八) noodles and tempura batter, creating a shared-environment cross-contamination risk even when the juwari (十割) noodle option is ordered. No source confirms dedicated equipment or separate preparation areas for buckwheat-only orders.

The tsuyu (dipping broth and hot soup base) is described as containing soy sauce (醤油) blended with bonito, mackerel, and skipjack dashi. Standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat; no tamari or GF soy sauce alternative has been mentioned by any source.

The dashi used in all soba broths is an animal-based blend (katsuobushi/skipjack, mackerel, bonito). Even the dashi-maki tamago (rolled omelet) is described as having a strong dashi flavour. There is no plant-based broth option confirmed.

No information about staff allergy training or allergy-handling procedures has been found in any source. Guests with celiac disease or severe wheat allergy should contact the restaurant directly before visiting.

A 十割 (juwari, 100% buckwheat flour) noodle option is available for +¥110. By recipe the noodles contain no added wheat flour, which may suit those with mild wheat sensitivity, though celiac-level safety cannot be confirmed given the shared kitchen environment.

name: 天ぷら かき揚げ 光村 (Tempura Kakiage Mitsumura)

claims.text: All tempura and kakiage — including vegetable items — are fried in the same sesame oil. No dedicated fryer for any allergen category is documented.
Tentsuyu dipping sauce and bowl tare are standard Japanese preparations that almost certainly contain wheat-based soy sauce; no tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere.
Vegetable tempura items share the frying oil with shrimp and fish tempura; no separation of cooking surfaces or oil confirmed.
No allergen menu, written allergy protocol, or English-language inquiry pathway has been documented on the official site or any third-party source reviewed.
Sesame oil is used for frying (not blended vegetable shortening), which some diners prefer for its distinct flavour profile and lower prevalence of certain seed allergens.

name: 手打蕎麦 ふたば (Teuchi Soba Futaba)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free preparation area is documented. The kitchen handles both wheat-containing nihachi noodles and tempura batter alongside the 100% buckwheat juwari soba, making cross-contamination a realistic concern for celiacs.
The tsuyu dipping broth and kakejiru hot broth are almost certainly made with standard soy sauce (which contains wheat) and bonito dashi — no wheat-free tamari alternative is mentioned anywhere.
Bonito-based dashi is the standard broth throughout; duck dishes are prepared in the same kitchen. No plant-based alternative broth has been confirmed.
No allergen handling procedures or staff allergy awareness information has been published for this restaurant. Phone ahead (052-522-5660) for any dietary requirements.

The juwari (十割) seiro uses 100% buckwheat flour with no wheat added to the noodle itself — the safest option on the menu for those avoiding wheat in the noodle strand, subject to kitchen cross-contamination caveats.

name: ザ バーキャッスル (THE BAR CASTLE)

claims.text: No information available on dedicated GF prep areas or cross-contamination controls. The kitchen produces wheat-containing pastry (scones, Atelier Ukai sweets) in the same kitchen context. Celiac diners should not assume safety.

Savory afternoon tea items (e.g., marinated tomatoes, soup, prosciutto preparations) are likely prepared with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat. No wheat-free soy sauce (tamari) is mentioned.
Afternoon tea is built around dairy-based pastries, clotted cream, and likely egg-containing sweets. No vegan-separated prep confirmed.

The venue asks guests to notify them of allergies or ingredients they cannot consume at time of reservation. They note they may be unable to accommodate requests made after arrival, and some requests may be declined prioritizing customer safety.

As part of a luxury international hotel, staff are accustomed to dietary-restriction conversations and communicate in English. Advance notice requests are built into their booking process via TableCheck and phone reservations.
Non-alcoholic cocktail alternatives are available for all bar items, and alcohol-free accommodations for dietary or lifestyle reasons are explicitly noted.
